one_liner: Google's API for creating, managing, and reporting on Search, Display, Video, Shopping, and Performance Max ad campaigns.
access_note: Anyone can self-serve a developer token with Test/Explorer Access instantly, but production use beyond ~2,880 ops/day requires a reviewed Basic Access application (5 business days), and unlimited use needs Standard Access (10 business days).
api_breadth_note: Full campaign, ad group, ad, keyword, bidding, audience, and reporting/GAQL coverage across all Google Ads campaign types.
existing_mcp_note: Google publishes an official read-only MCP server for diagnostics/analytics; several community servers also exist.
main_blocker: Developer token application review (Basic/Standard Access) plus OAuth2 client setup and Required Minimum Functionality compliance.

evidence.note: Official page detailing Test/Explorer/Basic/Standard access levels and review timelines.
Google's official MCP server page for Google Ads API.

researcher_notes: Basic Access (needed for most real automation) is a formal, reviewed application, not instant self-serve.

one_liner: Meta's Marketing API for creating, managing, and reporting on Facebook and Instagram ad campaigns.
access_note: Standard Access with ads_management/ads_read on your own ad account is usable without review, but managing other businesses' ad accounts or scaling requires Meta App Review and Business Verification.
api_breadth_note: Covers campaign/ad set/ad CRUD, targeting, creative, budgets, Insights/reporting, and Business Manager administration.
existing_mcp_note: No official Meta-published MCP server found; the most prominent is pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp.
main_blocker: App Review + Business Verification required for advanced permissions or managing accounts you don't own.

evidence.note: Permissions reference showing which scopes need App Review.
Community-built Meta Ads MCP server.

researcher_notes: 2026 policy reportedly requires minimum usage thresholds to reach/keep higher access tiers — should be re-verified directly.

one_liner: LinkedIn's Marketing API for creating and managing Campaign Manager ad campaigns, audiences, and analytics.
access_note: Only basic sign-in/share scopes are open to any registered developer; Marketing API (ads) access requires applying to LinkedIn's Marketing Developer Platform partner program, commonly taking weeks to months.
api_breadth_note: Covers campaign groups/campaigns/creatives, audiences, and analytics, but the whole surface sits behind partner approval.
existing_mcp_note: No official LinkedIn Ads MCP found; community servers exist but still require the developer's own approved credentials.
main_blocker: Marketing Developer Platform partner program application and review gates nearly all ads endpoints.

evidence.note: Getting Access to LinkedIn APIs page describing the partner program requirement.
LinkedIn Partner Programs application page.

researcher_notes: Approval SLA (weeks to months) should be verified directly on LinkedIn's own docs before being quoted as fact.

one_liner: All-in-one CRM, funnel, and marketing automation platform (contacts, pipelines, calendars, workflows, payments) built for agencies and SMBs.
access_note: A paid GoHighLevel (or agency/reseller) subscription is required to have an account at all; once you have one, API v2 credentials are self-serve from Marketplace/agency settings with no additional review.
api_breadth_note: Public API v2 covers contacts, opportunities/pipelines, calendars/appointments, conversations, workflows, payments/orders, and more.
existing_mcp_note: GoHighLevel ships an official MCP server (~21 tools), bundled free on Unlimited/SaaS Pro plans.

evidence.note: Official API v2 overview, OAuth2 auth model.
HighLevel Developer Portal describing app creation and Private Integration tokens.

researcher_notes: GoHighLevel has no free consumer tier — the platform itself is a paid product.

one_liner: Email marketing and marketing automation platform with audience, campaign, and e-commerce integrations.
access_note: Any Mailchimp account, including the free plan, can self-generate an API key immediately from account settings with no review.
api_breadth_note: Marketing API v3.0 covers audiences/contacts, campaigns, templates, automations, reports, e-commerce, and account exports.
existing_mcp_note: No official Marketing API MCP found (Mailchimp runs an official Transactional/Mandrill MCP); community Marketing API servers exist.

evidence.note: Confirms API key or OAuth2 auth, REST structure, free account can get an API key.
OAuth2 guide for third-party integrations.

researcher_notes: Feature depth can vary by paid plan tier, but the API itself is reachable from a free account.

one_liner: Email and SMS marketing automation platform for e-commerce, with segmentation, flows, and campaign management.
access_note: Free Klaviyo accounts can self-generate private API keys instantly in account settings with no review; most Marketing API functionality works on the free tier.
api_breadth_note: Covers profiles, events, campaigns, flows, segments, lists, catalogs, coupons, templates, and reporting.
existing_mcp_note: Klaviyo runs an official hosted remote MCP server, generally available to all customers since August 2025.

evidence.note: Confirms private API key, public key, and OAuth2 methods, plus per-endpoint scopes.
Official Klaviyo MCP server documentation.

researcher_notes: Klaviyo is actively migrating integrators from private-key auth to OAuth.

one_liner: All-in-one funnel builder, email marketing, and course platform aimed at solopreneurs and small businesses.
access_note: Free-tier systeme.io accounts can generate up to 3 public API keys directly from profile settings, with no application or review.
api_breadth_note: Public API covers contacts, tags, custom fields, funnels, price plans, coupons, and automation rules — notably smaller than the full product.
existing_mcp_note: systeme.io provides an official MCP server covering contacts, tags, newsletters, funnels, price plans, coupons, and automation rules.

evidence.note: Official public API reference.
Official MCP server setup guide.

researcher_notes: 'Narrow' breadth call is based on secondary summaries plus the official reference's visible resource list, not a line-by-line audit.

one_liner: Pinterest's API for managing Pins, boards, ad campaigns, catalogs, and analytics.
access_note: New apps default to a Trial Access tier that itself requires a Pinterest review; Standard/production access requires a further upgrade request and review.
api_breadth_note: Covers Pins, boards, ad campaigns, catalogs, and analytics/insights, but a meaningful subset of scopes (especially ads) is gated behind trial/standard access approval.
existing_mcp_note: No official Pinterest MCP found; community servers include clugtu/pinterest-mcp.
main_blocker: Trial access application/review is required before most non-trivial endpoints (including ads) become usable, plus a second review for Standard access.

evidence.note: OAuth2 grant types and access token setup.
App creation and trial-access request flow.

researcher_notes: Exact current review SLA should be double-checked directly on developers.pinterest.com.

one_liner: Meta's API for publishing posts/replies and reading insights on the Threads app.
access_note: Developers can post to their own account and registered testers immediately in development mode without review, but production for other users requires Meta App Review (~3-5 business days).
api_breadth_note: Covers publishing posts/replies/media, insights, and basic profile/mentions — much smaller than the broader Meta Graph API, no ads support.
existing_mcp_note: No official Threads MCP found; community servers include quinnjr/threads-mcp.
main_blocker: Meta App Review required to move beyond self/tester accounts into production for third-party use.

evidence.note: Threads API documentation hub (hint URL from task).
Community Threads MCP server example.

researcher_notes: Could not directly fetch developers.facebook.com/docs/threads in this session; recommend a direct fetch to confirm exact token lifetimes.

one_liner: Transactional and marketing email delivery API/platform, now part of Twilio.
access_note: SendGrid retired its permanent free tier in mid-2025; new accounts now get a 60-day trial (100 emails/day, no credit card) before requiring a paid plan starting at $19.95/month.
api_breadth_note: v3 REST API covers transactional email sending, marketing campaigns, templates, contacts/lists, stats/analytics, suppressions, and webhooks.
existing_mcp_note: No official SendGrid/Twilio MCP found; multiple community servers exist.

evidence.note: Official support article on the current 60-day trial account plan.
Current SendGrid product/pricing landing page (sendgrid.com now redirects to twilio.com).

researcher_notes: The classic 'free forever' 100/day plan referenced in older guides no longer exists as of mid-2025.
